title: Short-term Contract -> Perm: Probation Validation Canvas
body:
Purpose:
This working canvas documents a pragmatic, evidence-driven approach for evaluating short-term contractors (<= 6 months) for conversion to full-time. Intended audience: hiring manager, people ops partner, finance approver, and tech lead. This is a living doc — use it during the probation window and attach notes to the candidate record in HRIS (link above).

Scope & when to use:
- Use for contractors hired on fixed short-term engagements where conversion is being considered before or at the end of month 3 or 6.
- Not for interns or long-term contractors (>6 months) — separate intern-to-hire flow exists.

Core principles:
- Evidence over impression: prefer 3–5 discrete, linked signals rather than subjective summaries.
- Fast feedback loops: weekly quick-checks + deeper 30/60/90 reviews.
- Clear success criteria up front: manager and contractor agree on 3 measurable goals at start of conversion window.
- Risk-first mitigation: identify biggest conversion risks day 0 and plan remediation.

Timeline (example for 90-day conversion window):
- Day 0: Conversion-intent note added to contractor offer; manager and contractor create Conversion Goals doc (3 goals, metrics, owner, due date).
- Week 1: Kickoff 30-min align meeting (manager, tech lead, contractor, people ops). Capture role clarity and access needs.
- Weeks 2–4: Weekly 15-min syncs between manager and contractor (status + blockers) and one peer feedback contact.
- Day 30: First evaluation snapshot (manager score + peer signals + sample deliverables).
- Day 60: Midpoint check-in (score progress vs goals, remedial plan if needed).
- Day 85: Final evidence collection (artifact links, PR reviews, peer survey).
- Day 90: Decision meeting (manager, people ops, finance if needed). Decision recorded and next steps scheduled.

30-day success criteria (pick 3–5, required):
- Delivery signal: Delivered at least 1 scoped task end-to-end with QA or review completed.
- Collaboration: Ran or contributed to 2+ cross-team syncs or PR reviews with constructive comments.
- Ramp speed: demonstrated ability to use infra/dev tools autonomously (PR flow, CI, infra tickets).
- Communication: clear status updates and timely responses in Slack and standups.

Evaluation rubric (manager-facing, numeric):
- Score each dimension 1–5 (1 = major concern, 5 = exemplary). Aggregate to an overall signal used in decision: 12–15 pass; 8–11 conditional with defined remediation; <=7 escalate to people ops for alternative actions.
  Dimensions:
  - Delivery quality (code/doc/tests): 1–5
  - Ownership & velocity: 1–5
  - Teamwork & communication: 1–5
  - Learning / adaptability: 1–5
  - Culture & fit signals: 1–5
(Managers should add 1–2 sentences rationale per dimension and one concrete artifact link for each high/low score.)

Peer signal collection (fast pulse):
- One-question micro-survey sent to 3 peers after first month: 'Would you rely on this person to own an important piece of work for 2+ weeks? (Yes/Maybe/No)' + optional 1-sentence comment.
- Aggregate responses: 2+ Yes = positive peer signal; 2+ No = negative signal (requires follow-up).

Remediation playbook (if conditional):
- Trigger: aggregate rubric result in 'conditional' band or repeated peer concerns.
- 2-week focused remediation sprint that captures: specific outcomes to achieve, owner, checkpoints, and resources (mentor pairing, time allocation changes, training).
- Weekly review with manager + people ops; document outcome. If no material improvement by end of remediation sprint, convert to extension or non-conversion pathway.

Conversion decision matrix (simple):
- Pass (green): meets 3 core criteria + rubric aggregate >=12. Convert and prepare offer packet.
- Conditional (yellow): aggregate 8–11 OR mixed signals but manager believes in potential. Options: extend contract 30 days with remediation, or convert with development plan and probationary performance clause.
- Do not convert (red): aggregate <=7 OR critical infra/culture risks. Prepare offboarding timeline and knowledge transfer plan. Engage people ops to review final steps and payouts.

Operational checklist (attach links to artifacts in HRIS):
- [ ] Day 0: Conversion-intent flag set in contractor record
- [ ] Day 0: 3 conversion goals documented and shared
- [ ] Week 1: Kickoff notes uploaded to Confluence (owner: manager)
- [ ] Week 4: Peer micro-survey results attached
- [ ] Day 30: Manager rubric + sample artifact links attached
- [ ] Day 60: Midpoint update and remediation if any
- [ ] Day 85: Final artifact pack (PRs, docs, release notes) attached
- [ ] Decision recorded and next steps scheduled (conversion or offboarding)

Communication templates (short drafts):
- Manager -> candidate (early positive lean): 'Hey [Name], we're tracking good progress against goal X and appreciate how you handled Y. We'll do a formal 30-day review on [date] to collect artifacts and feedback.'
- People Ops -> finance (conversion request): 'Request approval to convert [Name] to FTE. Proposed base: [X]. Evidence pack: [link]. Recommended start: [date].'

Suggested evidence artifacts to include (link each):
- PRs and code reviews where the contractor authored or reviewed core work
- Design docs or runbooks the contractor contributed to
- A 15–30 minute demo recording of their core deliverable
- Peer micro-survey results and manager rubric notes

Edge cases & FAQs: 
- If contractor is primarily design/PM: swap 'PR' requirement with 2 stakeholder-aligned product artifacts and clear acceptance metrics.
- If conversion is driven by headcount freeze or budget: people ops will surface timing & comp constraints; document alternatives (extension, provisional conversion).
- If contractor declines conversion offer: capture reason, debrief, and if available, make plan to re-engage in future roles.

Decision paperwork & comp recommendation workflow:
- Manager completes 'Conversion Recommendation' form and attaches evidence. People ops reviews and sends compensation packet to finance/comp. If above-band, require remedial comp sign-off from Head of People + Head of Eng.

Notes to managers (best practices):
- Start with explicit success criteria with the contractor. Ambiguity kills conversions.
- Use short, time-boxed remediation sprints (not vague coaching).
- Keep record of decisions and evidence — we need these for equitable calibration and audit.

Appendix: Quick 15-min managers' checklist for the decision meeting:
- Look at rubric + peer pulse + top 3 artifacts
- Confirm whether the person reliably meets the team’s core workflow (tooling, communication, quality)
- Identify one hire-or-not rationale line and two development signals (if converting)
summary: Working canvas for evidence-based evaluation of short-term contractors for FTE conversion: timeline, rubric, peer signals, remediation, and operational checklist. Tailored for people ops + hiring managers to standardize decisions and reduce risk.
